title: Migrate Go web app Index handler from ParseFiles to inline html/template
description: Brownfield Go migration: replace the fragile runtime.Caller path-discovery + template.ParseFiles pattern with a package-level html/template variable parsed from an inline string.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate internal/handler/items.go. All existing tests must still pass. 1. Remove the templateDir() function and its imports (path/filepath, runtime). 2. Add a package-level var: var indexTmpl = template.Must(template.New("index").Parse(`...`)) with an inline template string that produces the same HTML structure: — DOCTYPE html, Items —

Item Catalogue

—
    with {{range .}}
  • {{.Name}} — ${{.Price}}
    • {{end}}
3. Rewrite Index() to use indexTmpl.Execute(w, Store) instead of ParseFiles. Keep Content-Type: text/html. 4. APIItems() is unchanged. All existing tests must still pass (Content-Type, status codes, JSON shape). Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Index() uses package-level template variable, not ParseFiles
runtime and path/filepath imports removed from items.go
Index() still sets Content-Type: text/html and returns 200
Template renders Item Name and Price
APIItems unchanged — all existing JSON tests pass
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
